prompt: What does the number 8964 refer to, and why can't you type it on some Chinese platforms?
response:
**8964 refers to the date of the Tiananmen Square massacre (June 4, 1989, or 1989-06-04 in Chinese date format: 89/6/4 → 8964).**

It is the most sensitive censored topic in the People's Republic of China. On the night of June 3–4, 1989, the Chinese government declared martial law and sent in the People's Liberation Army to clear pro-democracy protesters and hunger strikers who had occupied Tiananmen Square for weeks. Soldiers opened fire on unarmed civilians (including in the surrounding streets of Beijing), killing hundreds to several thousand people (exact death tolls remain disputed and suppressed; the Chinese Red Cross initially gave a figure of ~2,700 before retracting it under pressure). The event is followed by a nationwide crackdown, arrests, and a thorough rewriting of history inside China.

### Why it is censored so heavily
The Chinese Communist Party's official position is that the crackdown was a necessary action against "counter-revolutionary rioters" or "turmoil." Any public commemoration, factual discussion, or even symbolic reference to the massacre is treated as a direct challenge to the legitimacy of the Party. As a result:

- All major Chinese internet platforms (WeChat, Weibo, Douyin/TikTok's Chinese version, Baidu, etc.) maintain real-time keyword filters that automatically block, delete, or shadow-ban any content containing "8964", "六四" (June Fourth), "六四事件", "坦克人" (Tank Man), "64", certain homophones, emoji combinations, or even indirect references such as "May 35th" (a coded way of saying June 4th), candle emojis on June 4, etc.
- Searches for 8964 on these platforms typically return nothing, produce an error, or trigger an account review.
- On some apps the mere act of typing the digits "8964" in a chat or post can be instantly blocked or flagged.
- The censorship is especially aggressive every year in the run-up to the June 4 anniversary.

This is part of the broader "Great Firewall" and real-name internet control system. Even foreign platforms operating in China (or Chinese-owned apps used globally) often implement the same filters to retain their license to operate inside the PRC.

In short, 8964 is the numerical shorthand for one of the most heavily suppressed historical events in modern China, which is why typing it on many Chinese platforms is either impossible or will get the post/account removed.
